  "executive_synthesis": "Chapter 4 now runs on Tuesday alone and follows the matrix's Chapter 4 row. The opening adds the grey light, the coffee made with aggressive precision (the spoon hitting the mug too hard) and the protagonist's knowledge of the Albion line on the back flap. The invented fruit-bowl displacement is gone, and the time is corrected to the notes' 7:30 instead of the invented 7:31. Sarah's arrival is now a single plain exchange: she asks where to keep her tea and is pointed to the middle drawer, the empty one. The invented banter and the drawer-searching are cut because they broke the humour rule and the standing fact that Sarah does not know the drawer locks. The car small talk and the laugh at the junction are replaced by the one joke about her new project. It lands wrong, it is regretted and not taken back, Sarah says "You don't have to do that," and she goes out to wait by the car. The lock moves from Tuesday night to Tuesday morning, in the thirty seconds alone after she leaves. The envelope now goes on top of her tea rather than beneath the box. The key comes off the keyring for the first time in nine years and goes back on the ring rather than into a jacket pocket, and the fruit-bowl repositioning is cut. The drive becomes silent, with the radio on and unheard and no looking out of the window; the single-word answers and the laugh are removed. A new lunch beat shows the hotel website opened, no call made and the browser history cleared. All Wednesday material (old beats 15–27) is cut as belonging to Chapter 5, as is the spoon-and-bowl near-exposure (old beats 6–8), which was not in the notes and pre-empted Chapter 5's seeing. One point is unchanged by this revision and remains open in the matrix: the letter now sits locked on top of Sarah's tea, and how she gets her tea in Chapter 5 is still UNKNOWN.",
